To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a self-learning worm that uses importance scanning can be more virulent than a worm that uses other scanning methods, and a worm can learn the distribution of vulnerable targets by observing infected hosts.

a self-learning worm, which is a worm that learns and uses information about vulnerable hosts while spreading, can propagate faster than a worm using a fixed scanning strategy and that such a self-learning worm may be detected by observing the scanning patterns of the worm and the distribution of infected hosts.

(1) a self-learning worm that uses importance scanning can accurately estimate the distribution of vulnerable host and spread much faster than worms that use random scanning or permutation scanning; (2) such a worm is difficult to detect because the number of infected hosts that are observed by a defender is small and (3) a worm that uses importance-scanning is difficult to defend against because it is hard for a defender to know which scanning method a worm uses
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of worm propagation mechanisms and the resulting impact on worm propagation.
a new type of worm that can learn and exploit the distribution of vulnerable machines while it propagates.
the design of a self-learning worm, and the analysis of the worm's performance and the defense against it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a self-learning worm is a very powerful and efficient attack mechanism.
a self learning worm is a more effective worm than a random scanning worm, a permutation scanning worm, and a routing worm.
self-learning worms are more dangerous than worms using random scanning, and that the use of side information is a very effective way of increasing worm propagation speed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a self learning worm using importance scanning is a very powerful tool that can be used by an attacker to speed up the propagation of a worm.
a worm using importance scanning can propagate faster than a worm using any other scanning method.
the worm self-learning ability can help a worm spread faster, and that the worm self learning ability is a new and important threat to the Internet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of side information is a powerful tool to improve a worm's speed.
a worm that uses side information to speed up its propagation can be much more virulent than a random-scanner worm.
the worm scanning strategy can be learned from infected hosts, and the self-learning worm can be more virulent than other worms.
